title: Janax y Razar: un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador propios para un razonamiento artificial que piensa con melodías
description:
Janax is a hand-written operating system, language and assembler (all in assembly, no third-party engines) built to host Razar, an artificial reasoning system whose single judge is compression (two-part MDL). Version 0.6 is a research release about how far that judge reaches. (1) In C source code (the openrazer driver) Razar's sharpness wins 8 of 8 pre-registered antonyms and falls to chance when words are shuffled; in raw x86-64 machine code it does not engage. (2) On the bits of the kernel's executable code, without being told the word size, the same MDL principle picks 8-bit words aligned to the byte; a self-adjusting segmenter, with no rule about boundaries, learns 85 words of which 98.7% fall inside a single instruction (F1 0.369 against 0.255 on shuffled bytes and 0.235 at random); two earlier boundary rules failed and are reported. (3) Razar designs its organs by blind one-letter mutation; over the full landscape of its 819 organs of up to 3 letters it learns two recurring 'little towers' (16 and 38) from the organs that work, and none when the scores are shuffled. All predictions were written before running. Using the towers as building blocks for mutation is not yet tested. Documentation is in Spanish.

Janax es un sistema operativo, un idioma y un ensamblador escritos a mano en assembler, hechos para alojar a Razar. v0.6: el mismo juez de bits en código C, en los unos y los ceros del código máquina, y sobre los propios órganos de Razar (las torrecitas). Prototipo de investigación.
